thread:
tayla: Heads up — seeing requests in prod where the trace shows a req_id/span but there are no raw request log lines in the console for user-facing 500s. Anyone seen this pattern?

mike: Do you have a sample req_id and span link? timestamp + request example helps.

tayla: sample req: `01G8xyz9rQ` span link: https://console.redwood/trace/01G8xyz9rQ — the trace shows the full span tree and http attributes but when I grep the edge + workers logs the reqid doesn't appear.

devex-jen: Could be the ingress/edge not stamping the header consistently or the log-ingestion pipeline dropping malformed lines. Quick checks: run a stern search on the last 15m and also check ingestion parse errors. e.g.

```
stern -n prod "edge|proxy" --since 15m | rg "01G8xyz9rQ" -n
kubectl logs -n infra deploy/platform-logs-processor --since=20m | rg "parse error|01G8xyz9rQ"
```

tayla: ran the stern command — no hits. kubectl logs for platform-logs-processor shows a couple of `json.Unmarshal` errors around the same time.

mike: Are we using `x-request-ref` header or `x-request-id` for correlation? mismatch there will make console lookups fail even if spans have the id.

kai: Traces having the id but logs missing usually means either: 1) the service emitted a truncated/malformed log and the parser dropped it, or 2) the header key used by the service is different from what the ingestion pipeline extracts. Check the span attrs to confirm header key.

tayla: span http.request.headers shows "x-request-ref":"01G8xyz9rQ". so header is there. processor parse errors look like this: `json.Unmarshal error: invalid character '}' looking for beginning of object` for the same time window.

ops-bot: ALERT: platform-logs-processor parse-error-rate spike detected at 15:42 UTC — dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/d/logs/processor-errors

tayla: ok that's the smoking gun — lines were dropped. looks like a downstream service logs a truncated JSON when body size is big, causing the line to be rejected. rolling a tolerant parser in a tiny PR now. PR: https://git.redwood/infra/platform-logs-processor/pulls/456

mike: Short-term hunting tip: if console raw-lines are missing, you can still use the trace UI to see associated events and headers (open trace -> events -> http.request). Or use the CLI trace fetch: `rb trace get 01G8xyz9rQ --raw` — that often surfaces the request attrs even when logs are gone.

devex-jen: Nice. When you ship the parser fix, please also add an eval and dashboard panel for parse-error-rate + a tiny alert (e.g. >5/min) so we catch this earlier. I'll add the dashboard tile and an alert rule.

eng-sre-oncall: If you need immediate recovery for customers, we can temporarily lower the ingestion strictness to accept partial JSON as raw and forward it to a dead-letter bucket for reprocessing. Lemme know and we'll run the change during the next quiet window.

tayla: thanks — I'm merging the PR after a quick unit test. will ping here when it's on prod and when I add the eval. :thumbsup:
